# Psalms of Solomon — Psalm 18 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Vindobonensis) | **Section:** The LORD's Messiah — Blessed Are Those Born in Those Days

---

**18:1** O LORD, your mercy reaches over all the works of your hands forever;
your goodness covers Israel like a lavish gift.

**18:2** Your eyes are on them — not one of them is left in want;
your ears are open to the hopeful prayer of the poor.

**18:3** Your judgments reach over all the earth in mercy;
your love rests upon the seed of Abraham, the children of Israel.

**18:4** Your discipline falls on us as on a firstborn, an only child —
to turn the obedient soul back from a sin it did not know it had done.

**18:5** May God purify Israel for the day of mercy and blessing,
for the day of his choosing when he brings back his anointed.

**18:6** Blessed are those who will live in those days,
to see the good things the LORD will do
for the generation yet to come —

**18:7** under the rod of discipline of the LORD's anointed,
in the fear of his God,
in the spirit of wisdom and righteousness and strength —

**18:8** guiding every person in righteous deeds through the fear of God,
establishing them all before the LORD:

**18:9** a good generation, living in the fear of God,
in the days of his mercy.

**18:10** Great is our God and glorious,
enthroned in the highest heaven.

**18:11** He set the lights of heaven in their courses
to mark off the seasons year after year;

**18:12** they have not turned aside from the course he set them;
they run their course day after day in the fear of God.

**18:13** From the day of their creation and forever —
they have not strayed since the day he made them,
through all the generations of ancient time.

**18:14** They have never deviated from their course
except when God commanded it through the word of his servants.

---

*PNEUMA notes: Dynamic rendering of Ps 18. The final psalm echoes the great themes: God's mercy, the anointed one's discipline, the obedient cosmos. The stars that keep their courses are an image of the coming age of perfect order.*
